literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 该研究证明了设计的 疫苗 与 TLR2、TLR3、TLR4 和 TLR7 的显着亲和力,并通过分子动力学模拟验证了详细的氢键相互作用。疫苗 触发了强大的先天性和适应性 免疫应答,IFN-γ 和 IL-2 的产生证明了这一点,并且在 宿主 的整个表达途径中保持稳定。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0361136]
在调整后的分析中,地点是血清反应性的主要预测因素,蒙加拉省和楚阿帕省的 BDBV 血清反应性几率比奎卢省高 9.1 倍(95% CI 7.0-11.9)和 9.5 倍(95% CI 6.9-13.2)。 [10.64898/2026.10.20.26366019]
2026-10-23发表的《通过结构动力学和免疫模拟分析,针对 马尔堡病毒 自扩增 RNA 疫苗 进行免疫信息学和反向疫苗学设计》进入本期重点文献清单，详细证据见下方单篇解读。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0361136]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The study demonstrated significant affinity of the designed vaccines to TLR2, TLR3, TLR4, and TLR7, with detailed hydrogen-bond interactions validated by molecular dynamics simulations. [10.1371/journal.pone.0361136]

In adjusted analyses, site was the primary predictor of seroreactivity, with odds for BDBV seroreactivity 9.1-fold (95%CI 7.0-11.9) and 9.5-fold (95%CI 6.9-13.2) higher in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces than in Kwilu. [10.64898/2026.10.20.26366019]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
该研究证明了设计的 疫苗 与 TLR2、TLR3、TLR4 和 TLR7 的显着亲和力,并通过分子动力学模拟验证了详细的氢键相互作用。疫苗 触发了强大的先天性和适应性 免疫应答,IFN-γ 和 IL-2 的产生证明了这一点,并且在 宿主 的整个表达途径中保持稳定。

papers.title: Immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology design of self-amplifying RNA vaccine against marburg virus with structural dynamics and immune simulation analysis
papers.abstract: Marburg virus disease (MVD), a deadly zoonotic illness in humans, is caused by the Marburg virus (MARV), a single-stranded RNA virus belonging to the Orthomarburgvirus genus of the Filoviridae family. There are currently no approved vaccines or efficient antiviral therapies for MARV, despite high morbidity and fatality rates of the virus, particularly in Africa. Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI < 7), soluble (GRAVY < 0), and stable (aliphatic index < 80). Subsequently, docking of MB-saVaxI to TLR2 (-938.3) and TLR4 (-902.4), and MB-saVaxII to TLR3 (-1485.4) and TLR7 (-1543.6) demonstrated significant affinity, with detailed hydrogen-bond interactions validated by MM-GBSA and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were effectively cloned in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.

Recognizing its epidemic potential and its inclusion on the WHO list of blueprint priority pathogens, an immunoinformatics approach was used to design novel multi-epitope saRNA vaccine candidates (MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII) targeting the viral GP, NP, VP40, and VP35 via CD8 + , CD4 + , and B cell epitopes. These epitopes were derived from target protein sequences and incorporated into MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII after validation for antigenicity, non-allergenicity, non-toxicity, and conservation. Additionally, the selected epitopes were conjugated to suitable adjuvants via various linkers, thereby enabling the design of a potentially stable vaccine. Additionally, the designed MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were incorporated into the standard saRNA model, in which ORF-2 encodes the target vaccine peptide. Moreover, biophysical analyses unveiled that the developed vaccines are basic (pI < 7), soluble (GRAVY < 0), and stable (aliphatic index < 80). Subsequently, docking of MB-saVaxI to TLR2 (-938.3) and TLR4 (-902.4), and MB-saVaxII to TLR3 (-1485.4) and TLR7 (-1543.6) demonstrated significant affinity, with detailed hydrogen-bond interactions validated by MM-GBSA and molecular dynamics simulations. Furthermore, MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII were effectively cloned in-silico into Escherichia coli, and immune simulations indicated that the vaccines triggered robust innate and adaptive immunity, with a sustained memory response and TH cell activation, as evidenced by IFN-γ and IL-2 production. Additionally, the mRNA structure of MB-saVaxI and MB-saVaxII remained stable throughout the expression pathway in the host. However, extensive in-vitro and in-vivo studies are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of this vaccine candidate conclusively.

papers.title: Filovirus Seroreactivity Beyond Virus-Specific Outbreak Regions in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2015-2023
papers.abstract: The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second-largest Ebola disease outbreak in recorded history, and only the second recorded BVD outbreak in the country. papers.title_zh: 丝状病毒 刚果民主共和国病毒特异性 暴发 区域以外的血清反应性,2015-2023 年
papers.source_body_en: The ongoing Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is the second-largest Ebola disease outbreak in recorded history, and only the second recorded BVD outbreak in the country. While the DRC has recorded 18 filovirus disease outbreaks, the historical frequency and geographic distribution of human filovirus exposures remain poorly understood. Using a multiplexed multi-filovirus immunoassay, we assessed antibody reactivity against antigens of filoviruses linked to human disease, Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), Ebola virus (EBOV), Marburg virus (MARV), and Sudan virus (SUDV), among eleven cohorts from seven provinces between 2015-2023 (n=5,852). Participants with median fluorescence intensity values exceeding established antigen-specific cutoffs were classified as seroreactive. Seroreactivity against glycoprotein (GP) targets of all four viruses were detected in every cohort, demonstrating evidence of filovirus or an antigenically related exposure well beyond known outbreak regions. Seroreactivity estimates varied by cohort site, with 60.8% of participants (n=175/288) in Mongala Province in April 2016 considered seroreactive against BDBV GP. In this cohort, 4.2%, 29.9%, and 34.7% of participants were seroreactive against EBOV, MARV and SUDV GP, respectively yet only 1.7% were seroreactive against all four GP antigens. In adjusted analyses, site was the primary predictor of seroreactivity, with odds for BDBV seroreactivity 9.1-fold (95%CI 7.0-11.9) and 9.5-fold (95%CI 6.9-13.2) higher in Mongala and Tshuapa provinces than in Kwilu. Similarly, the adjusted odds of MARV and SUDV GP seroreactivity were 4.5-fold and 7.1-fold higher in Mongala, and 3.7-fold and 6.1-fold higher in Tshuapa, than Kwilu. Among 280 individuals sampled longitudinally, BDBV GP detected seroconversion was comparable by site, with 12.8% in Kwilu and 10.4% in Mongala having detected seroreactivity three and five years after initial contact, respectively. Overall, these results indicate widespread, geographically heterogeneous filovirus seroreactivity across sampled cohorts. These findings may reflect zoonotic spillover events, leading to undetected human-to-human filovirus circulation, including paucisymptomatic or asymptomatic infections, or exposure to as-yet unidentified antigenically cross-reactive viruses. These data highlight gaps in understanding the historical and geographic distribution of filovirus exposure in the DRC and support further prospective serological, epidemiological, and molecular investigations, especially given the current outbreak.
papers.abstract_zh: 刚果民主共和国(DRC)正在发生的本迪布焦病毒病(BVD)ZX​​QTERMXQXZ是有记录以来第二大埃博拉病毒病暴发,也是该国仅有第二记录的BVD 暴发。虽然刚果民主共和国已记录了 18 种 丝状病毒 疾病 丝状病毒,但人类 丝状病毒 暴露的历史频率和地理分布仍然知之甚少。使用多重 丝状病毒 免疫测定,我们评估了 2015 年至 2023 年间来自七个省的 11 个 队列研究 中与人类疾病、本迪布焦病毒 (BDBV)、埃博拉病毒 (EBOV)、马尔堡病毒 (MARV) 和苏丹病毒 (SUDV) 相关的 丝状病毒 抗原的抗体反应性 (n=5,852)。荧光强度中值超过既定抗原特异性截止值的参与者被归类为血清反应性。在每个 队列研究 中均检测到所有四种病毒针对糖蛋白 (GP) 靶标的血清反应性,证明了 丝状病毒 或抗原相关暴露远远超出已知 暴发 区域的证据。血清反应性估计因 队列研究 站点而异,2016 年 4 月蒙加拉省 60.8% 的参与者 (n=175/288) 被认为对 BDBV GP 有血清反应性。在该 队列研究 中,分别有 4.2%、29.9% 和 34.7% 的参与者对 EBOV、MARV 和 SUDV GP 呈血清反应,但只有 1.7% 对所有四种 GP 抗原呈血清反应。在调整后的分析中,地点是血清反应性的主要预测因素,蒙加拉省和楚阿帕省的 BDBV 血清反应性几率比奎卢省高 9.1 倍(95% CI 7.0-11.9)和 9.5 倍(95% CI 6.9-13.2)。同样,Mongala 地区 MARV 和 SUDV GP 血清反应性的调整后赔率比 Kwilu 地区高 4.5 倍和 7.1 倍,Tshuapa 地区高 3.7 倍和 6.1 倍。在纵向采样的 280 名个体中,BDBV GP 检测到的血清转化率在不同地点具有可比性,奎卢 (Kwilu) 和蒙加拉 (Mongala) 分别有 12.8% 和 10.4% 在初次接触后三年和五年内检测到血清反应性。总体而言,这些结果表明 丝状病毒 样本中存在广泛的、地理上异质的 丝状病毒 血清反应性。这些发现可能反映了人畜共患 跨物种溢出 事件,导致未检测到的人际 丝状病毒 循环,包括少症状或无症状感染,或暴露于尚未鉴定的抗原交叉反应病毒。这些数据凸显了在了解刚果民主共和国 丝状病毒 暴露的历史和地理分布方面的差距,并支持进一步的前瞻性血清学、流行病学和分子研究,特别是考虑到当前的 暴发。

Advertisement IDWeek 2-26 in Washington, DC (Adobe Stock) A systematic review presented as a poster at IDWeek in Washington, DC, held from October 21 to 24, found that transmission of viral hemorrhagic fevers to health care personnel in high-income countries was rare. Across 35 studies, presenting author Loukas Kakoullis, MD, PhD, MPH, Infectious Disease Fellow at Massachusetts General Hospital & Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, and his fellow researchers reported 1,607 health care personnel exposures and 37 infections, an infection proportion of 2.3%. SelectScience CLINICAL24 2026 Home /News NewsClinical Diagnostics WHO emergency use listing expands access to BIOFIRE Global Fever Panel for Ebola diagnostics bioMérieux 20 Oct 2026 Summary: bioMérieux’s BIOFIRE® Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel has received World Health Organization Emergency Use Listing, expanding access to rapid differential diagnostic testing for the ongoing Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and neighbouring countries. The molecular diagnostic test can detect 16 pathogens, including multiple Ebola viruses, malaria parasites, Marburg virus, West Nile virus and Lassa virus, from a single whole blood sample in approximately one hour, helping healthcare professionals identify suspected cases, guide patient management and strengthen outbreak response. bioMérieux, a world leader in in vitro diagnostics, has announced that the World Health Organization (WHO) has granted Emergency Use Listing (EUL) for the BIOFIRE® Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel, strengthening access to differential diagnostic testing in support of the ongoing Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak affecting the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighboring countries. The WHO listing comes as national health authorities, international organizations and local partners continue efforts to contain one of the largest outbreaks ever recorded of Ebola virus. While no specific treatment or licensed vaccine has been developed against the Bundibugyo strain, fast and accurate diagnostic testing exists and remains the first line of public health action to identify suspected cases, guide patient management, support contact tracing and help limit disease transmission. Manufactured by BioFire Defense, LLC, a bioMérieux company, the BIOFIRE® Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel enables healthcare professionals to simultaneously test for 16 pathogens from a single whole blood sample in approximately one hour, including multiple Ebola viruses, malaria parasites, Marburg virus, West Nile virus and Lassa virus. By helping differentiate Ebola from other causes of acute febrile illness with similar symptoms, the panel supports faster clinical decision making and more effective use of limited healthcare resources. The WHO Emergency Use Listing serves as an international reference providing an additional accelerated pathway for health authorities, international organizations and procurement partners to consider the panel as part of the response to the current outbreak and future preparedness efforts. “The WHO Emergency Use Listing is an important milestone for public health preparedness and outbreak response," said Dr. Charles K. Cooper, Executive Vice President, Chief Medical Officer, bioMérieux. "When an outbreak occurs, early and accurate diagnosis can make the difference between isolated cases and wider transmission. Expanding access to timely differential diagnostics helps healthcare professionals act more quickly, allocate resources more effectively and better protect communities." Importantly, the panel includes detection of Bundibugyo ebolavirus, the strain responsible for the current outbreak. This capability was developed years before the emergence of the current epidemic as part of BioFire Defense's long-term commitment to protecting against biothreats and emerging infectious diseases. Supporting health authorities to reinforce diagnostics capabilities Since the beginning of the outbreak, bioMérieux has worked alongside Ministries of Health, public health agencies and local partners to assess diagnostic needs, strengthen laboratory capacity and support deployment of testing resources across affected regions. The company has expanded manufacturing capacity, accelerated deliveries of instruments and tests, and provided training and on-site support to laboratory professionals to help ensure rapid implementation and sustainable diagnostic capabilities. bioMérieux has already delivered instruments and reagents to the Rwanda Biomedical Centre in June, together with training and implementation support for laboratory teams. bioMérieux also supported Uganda preparedness by delivering Instruments and reagents to the Uganda National Health Laboratory Services. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, bioMérieux is working with the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB) and health authorities to provide additional instruments and tests. These contributions are intended to complement existing diagnostic capabilities and support the use of molecular differential testing when further investigation of suspected cases is required. "Outbreak response is about more than delivering tests," stated Vanina Laurent-Ledru Chief Public Health and Government Affairs Officer, bioMérieux. "It requires strong partnerships, trained healthcare professionals, laboratory capacity and sustained surveillance systems. Our goal is to support health authorities not only in addressing today's outbreak, but also in strengthening preparedness for future health threats.” The BIOFIRE® Global Fever Special Pathogens Panel is FDA-cleared. It is also recommended by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) for response to the current outbreak. Want the latest science news straight to your inbox?
